statusText: Mapped policy state: EA_ON. Tail remains low because current evidence does not establish a persistent no-retracement Nasdaq-100 path.
recommendation: Current Tail remains below the block threshold; the principal conditional risk window is the U.S. cash open and flash-PMI/post-release sequence.
headline: Low Tail with extreme macro and rates stress; the U.S. open and PMI remain the main conditional risk window.
body: Reuters reported Nasdaq futures steady while Asian technology shares advanced, oil eased and the U.S. 2-year yield recently reached 4.7879%. Public delayed NQ pages differ on exact session framing, so granular pullback quality is not independently verified. No persistent no-mean-reversion path is established.

lookbackSummary: Across the prior 24 published hourly assessments, Tail was mostly low, rose to WATCH in the Europe/U.S. transition, peaked at 27% around the U.S. open, then fell back as retracement and mixed structure emerged. Stress stayed extreme for most of the period.
outlookSummary: The next 24 hours remain low-Tail in the base case outside a narrow 13:30-15:30 UTC U.S. open/PMI/Fed/EIA window. Forecast Tail rises only conditionally if opening direction persists through weak retracements or a coherent second leg; it should recede if two-way discovery returns.

forecast.analysis: Liquidity and positioning can become less stable ahead of the 13:30 cash open and 13:45 flash PMI. WATCH-level Tail is conditional on futures holding an extreme and rejecting meaningful pullbacks before the release.

This hour contains the 13:30 U.S. cash open and 13:45 flash PMI. Elevated forecast Tail is conditional on opening-auction direction persisting through the release with shallow pullbacks, failed retracements or repeated extension.

The first full post-PMI hour also includes Governor Barr at 14:05 UTC and EIA petroleum data at 14:30 UTC. Tail stays elevated only if price discovery produces a coherent second leg and resists meaningful mean reversion.
Two-way price discovery would lower Tail toward WATCH in this hour. Persistent extreme-holding after the release cluster would instead keep the danger window active through 15:30 UTC.
After the scheduled cluster, Tail should recede if pullbacks deepen and cross-assets stabilize. Continued one-way extension without meaningful retracement would keep risk above the low band.
Late-afternoon U.S. trading should normalize further if the event impulse is absorbed. Tail stays at WATCH only if the market continues to reject retracements and hold near session extremes.
Tail returns to the low band if the U.S. afternoon develops balanced trade. A new directional catalyst would need fresh confirmation before changing the path assessment.
drivers: Fresh confirmation required for renewed Tail escalation

forecast.analysis: As Europe closes and U.S. trading continues, the base case favors lower Stress and low Tail. Any late-session trend would need repeated extension and weak pullbacks to become materially pathological.
Late U.S. afternoon risk is lower in the base case, although headline sensitivity remains. Tail stays low unless momentum becomes one-way with little retracement.
The final cash-session hour can produce position adjustments, but no pathological path is assumed. Tail remains low unless a closing drive repeatedly extends and holds its extreme.
After the cash close, price discovery typically thins. Tail remains low if futures consolidate; a fresh headline-driven break would require new evidence rather than being assumed in advance.
drivers: Fresh headline evidence required for any break

forecast.analysis: Early Globex conditions favor a low-Tail baseline if the post-close range holds. Stress continues to ease absent a new cross-asset shock.
drivers: Conditional absence of a fresh cross-asset shock

forecast.analysis: Overnight trade remains low-Tail in the base case. The next U.S. claims and housing releases are many hours away, so only a verified directional break would justify a material Tail increase.

drivers: Persistence matters more than move size
